question:
Seven boxes F, G, H, I, K, L and O are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order.

O is kept second from the bottom. Only three boxes are kept between O and G. L is kept at one of the positions below O. Only I is kept between G and H. F is kept at one of the positions above G.

How many boxes are kept between L and F?
solution:
Given: Seven boxes F, G, H, I, K, L and O are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order.

1) O is kept second from the bottom.

2) Only three boxes are kept between O and G.

3) L is kept at one of the positions below O.

4) Only I is kept between G and H.

5) F is kept at one of the positions above G.
